reading.body:
Box has built a portfolio of integrations that let AI agents handle real-world tasks: sending physical mail, managing cloud files, accessing bank data, and exchanging secrets between agents.

These Model Context Protocol tools sit at the boundary between AI systems and the infrastructure they need to operate at scale. An AI agent that can only think cannot process a loan application or onboard an employee. It must read files, verify identity, send documents, and maintain audit trails. Box's integrations bridge this gap by giving agents standardized access to storage, communication channels, and cross-agent coordination. The company's own AI product focuses on enterprise content, but this MCP registry strategy positions it as an operational layer for agentic workflows, where the binding constraint shifts from model capability to the ability to act on real data and systems.

What these integrations do not show is compute or power consumption. They are software abstractions that assume infrastructure exists elsewhere. They do show that AI scaling now depends not only on larger models and more training compute, but on standardized ways for agents to access the human-world interfaces they need to do work. For enterprises, this means the grid constraint on AI is mediated through the systems that connect agents to email, filesystems, banks, and each other.

profile_text.body:
Box is a publicly traded company (NYSE: BOX) founded in 2005 and headquartered in Redwood City, California. The company describes itself as offering an Intelligent Content Management platform that brings together workflow automation, collaboration, and data security in a single system. Its site positions unstructured data, such as lease agreements, finance documents, sales presentations, and employee handbooks, as central to the work it supports, and emphasizes that teams inside and outside an organization can access, share, edit, and co-create content from anywhere.

Box AI is the company's primary AI product, tracked under the Notes, Knowledge, and Meetings category, covering enterprise content AI, metadata, governance, compliance, and retention policies. The site describes Box AI as drawing on models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google to deliver real-time summaries, deep analysis, and smart recommendations across enterprise content. The platform also includes Box AI Studio for customizing agents and building agentic workflows, a drag-and-drop workflow builder for automating processes such as loan processing and employee onboarding, AI-driven security features including deep learning-based malware detection and automated data classification, built-in compliance tools for standards such as GDPR, HIPAA, and FINRA, and unlimited e-signatures described as included at no additional cost.

Box's most recently reported annual revenue, from its 10-K filing for the period ending January 31, 2026, was $1,177,253,000. The held facts show 181 California law exposure entries on record and no litigation cases currently tracked for the company. The MCP registry entries associated with Box in the held data belong to third-party tools and do not represent Box's own MCP server offerings.
